decisions.issues: Minor only: the yard figures mostly face the house rather than clearly looking up at the wall, and the fort flies a plain white flag instead of the Travancore conch-on-red standard (the same white flag appears in panels 2, 4 and 5, so the page is consistent). Ridges, red earth, gold grass, village smoke, laterite wall behind bamboo scaffolding with masons, and the tiled house among pepper vines all match. No text, gore or anachronism. Large clear sky at upper left for both captions.

Minor only. A thin maroon cord, read as a sword belt, shows at the waist under the mundu folds. It is not a broad red sash. The trader's towel is on his right shoulder here and on his left in panel 1.3. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain, talwar at his left hip, cream shoulder cloth. The trader matches the script: grey beard, bare head and chest, checked lungi, towel, clay cup, talking up at Nagoji. The flag is plain white and the art has no text. Open sky at upper centre and upper right leaves room for all three balloons.

The trader does not quite match panel 1.2. Here he has short curly grey hair, a close-trimmed beard and a heavier build. In 1.2 his hair is longer and swept back, and his beard is fuller. His towel has also moved to the other shoulder. He is not a principal, he still fits the script description, and the reader can take him as the same man, so this is acceptable. The beat works: he is close, shrugs with an open palm and holds a clay cup of buttermilk. The courtyard, laterite wall and tiled verandah match 1.2. The oil lamp is clay with an open flame. Both hands are sound and there is no text. Clear sky in the upper right gives room for the long and medium balloons, away from his face and the shrugging hand.

Acceptable, with minor deviations: Ramayyan writes with a stylus on the palm-leaf bundle instead of tapping his fingers on it. Varma's hair knot sits low at the back of his head behind the near (right) ear rather than as a side knot above the left ear, though he is clearly bare-headed with no turban or crest. Varma looks off-panel to the right instead of straight at the reader, which still works spatially because the courtyard where Nagoji stood in panel 1.2 lies to the right of the verandah. Both faces match their sheets. Hands are sound. No text. The hanging brass lamp has an open wick. Clear sky at upper right, and a plain wall with roof beams at upper left, give room for both Ramayyan balloons.

Clean. The face matches the V13 Varma sheet: thick moustache, pearl drop earrings and gold bead necklaces. He is bare-headed with his hair in a knot above and behind his LEFT ear, with no turban, crest or crown. He is bare-chested under a cream cloth with a gold border. The border pattern is geometric, not pseudo-text. There is no bandage, which is correct because the knife wound comes later in the chapter. He shows a faint amused smirk, set in the same laterite courtyard and verandah. Open sky in the upper left takes both balloons clear of his face.

Clean on the main checks. Nagoji has a topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small round gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it, a silver chain, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. He rides Kayal, a bay with black points and no white markings. Padmini rides beside him in a cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, with simple gold, the thick hair coiled at the nape and the staff laid across her saddle. The column is all there: turbaned riders with tall spears on dark horses, musketeers in white on foot with long matchlocks, and a brass light gun on a carriage with bullocks, on a red dirt track. There is no text, blood or European kit, and the large clear sky upper right holds both the caption and the balloon. Minor points: Padmini's hair is more grey than 'black threaded with grey'. Her staff is a turned pole with brass bands, where her sheet shows a knobbly natural stick, so at a glance it reads a little like a musket barrel. She and Nagoji wear riding boots. The Nair musketeers wear turbans, where bare-headed topknots would be more accurate. The forearm scar is not visible. None of these is disqualifying.

Minor: Padmini's hair reads almost all black in the dusk light, with little of the grey threading that the ch16-27 row and the neighbouring panels 2.1 and 2.5 show. Everything else matches the beat: a Kerala gatehouse with a low tiled roof and carved gable figures, cloths between trees, wall-niche oil lamps, drummers and pipers, girls carrying the flower-decked goddess palanquin, older women with brass plates, Padmini dismounted in the line with a clay lamp and her stick, and men bowing. No painted text. Clear dusk sky at top centre for the caption.

Minor: the brand patch and long white scar are correctly on Nagoji's LEFT forearm, but they sit on the outer side near the elbow rather than on the inner forearm a hand's width above the wrist, and there is an extra long pale scar on his left upper arm. Ponnan has a tiny ear stud, and his horse is the same size as Kayal rather than a head lower. These are small. Nagoji matches his sheet (topknot, grey temples, gold ear stud, clean chin, thick curled moustache, silver chain), and so does Ponnan (curly hair, no topknot, moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear). The tusker with its gold nettipattam and children offering bananas is present. Dusk sky across the top centre takes both balloons above the heads.

Minor: the sweet fried discs are drawn as glazed rings that look a little like pretzels, though they pass as fried festival sweets. Yusuf matches the bible (tall, lean, white skullcap, trimmed dark beard, short dark coat over a white tunic, no turban, no scar). He keeps one hand on the basket, steadies the startled boy with the other and smiles up toward someone out of frame. Same festival setting, lamps and elephant as 2.2 and 2.3. Open sky at upper left and centre takes both captions.

Page continuity: Padmini's horse has a broad white blaze and a lighter reddish coat, while in 2.1 v01 she rides a plain dark bay. The 2.1 correction asks for the blaze, so the two will match after regeneration. Otherwise this matches the beat: Padmini back at her horse with lamp-lit wall and the procession behind her, eyes bright, grey-threaded hair, gold, cream sari with gold border and her stick. No painted text, and the hands on the bridle and stick are sound. The dusk sky and trees at top centre can take her balloon clear of her face.

Minor only. Nagoji matches: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, no turban or red sash. He wears a sheathed sword at the hip, which is not a knife. Kayal is a bay with black points and no white markings. Ponnan matches (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, spear) but wears an ochre jacket, while in 3.4 he wears a red, gold-trimmed tunic as on his sheet. The covered dead wear heavy leather boots and belts that read a little soldierly, but no faces or blood show. The large clear sky at upper right takes both Ponnan balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji stands dismounted, while 3.1 shows him mounted; the script does not specify either way. A faint shadow of stubble on the chin still reads as clean-shaven. The checked cloth and coins lie on the ground instead of in Ponnan's hand. A round brand and scar show on the left forearm, which the ch23 bible row allows. Otherwise the panel matches: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, silver chain, raided convoy setting, and a gaze toward the hills. The sky top centre and right is clear for both balloons.

Clean. Spearmen and archers stand across the road, with matchlockmen on both slopes holding smoking slow-match at their wrists. The plain green banners carry no writing, and the raja sits on a low stool in the centre of the road. He is drawn a little larger than 'very small' but still reads as distant. Some raiders wear white head cloths. The pale sky between the slopes is clear for both captions.

Minor only. The shot is over the shoulder from behind Nagoji: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth, inclined head, with Kayal's bay ears and black mane below. Ponnan's spear and red cloth are at the left edge. The grey-haired, grey-moustached, bare-chested Nair captain with a round shield is at the right edge. The raja sits centred, facing us, heavy, with gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword at the sash, and he does not rise. Ponnan's visible sleeve is a red, gold-trimmed tunic (his sheet look), unlike the ochre jacket in 3.1. Nagoji's tail point is his hidden mouth beside the ear, since he faces away. The sky between the banners is clear for three balloons.

Minor only. The raja spreads his hands, at ease on his stool, with grinning spearmen behind and matchlockmen and plain green banners on the slopes. He shows gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword at the sash. His chin carries a light dark stubble that is not in 3.4. His second foot is hidden under the long mundu. The ground is redder than the pale road in 3.3 and 3.4. Nagoji speaks from off panel, and the raja glances to the viewer's left, so that line's tail points to the left frame edge. The large open sky takes all three balloons.

Clean pick. It is a true close-up, as the r1 correction asked. Brows are lowered, the lids narrowed a fraction and the eyes cut sideways. He has long black hair swept back loose with no bun, a thick moustache, a clean chin, heavy gold ear hoops, several neck chains and a bare chest. Behind him are a red-earth slope, a plain green banner and spearmen in indigo head cloths. The upper-left third is open blue sky for both balloons, and there is no text. Minor: his eyes cut toward frame right, not frame left, so the off-panel Nagoji tail points to the upper right edge. One barely visible figure at the far right edge has a reddish head cloth.

Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failures. There is no stool in the road and no yellow flags. The slope men are bare-chested in indigo head cloths under plain green banners, and the foreground musketman's matchlock glows correctly at the lock, not at the muzzle. Nagoji has the topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, cream shoulder cloth with gold border over his left shoulder and the silver chain. His open palm is raised and his eyes are not on Ponnan. Ponnan has curly hair, a moustache, the red shoulder cloth, a short jacket and a spear, on a smaller horse. Kayal is bay with a black mane. Minor points: Nagoji's ear stud is a tiny gold bead at the lobe, which still reads as a stud. Faint pale streaks on his raised RIGHT inner forearm could read as a scar on the wrong arm, but they are only a few pixels. The distant column behind the riders wears dark head cloths with crossed belts and carries spears, a little unlike the white-turbaned Nairs of 4.3. A few distant slope men wear dark vests. There is sky at top centre and right for the two balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji wears a dark shoe in the stirrup. His gesture back toward the column is a thumb jerked over the shoulder, which reads a little casual. A small red banner hangs in the middle distance, but it sits with the Travancore column and is not on a raider. Nagoji otherwise matches his sheet: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear studs and a silver chain. He has no turban and no red sash. Kayal is bay with black points and no white markings. The raja's bare back, gold-edged sash, hoop and sword are in the foreground. The Nair musketeers and the gun on its bullock carriage are behind Nagoji, and matchlocks frame both slopes. The open sky across the upper centre gives clear space for both of Nagoji's balloons.

Clean pick. The raja leans forward on the stool with a clenched scowl. His look is right: bare chest, gold ear hoops and chains, gold-edged sash, worn-hilted sword. The slopes are consistent with page 3 (matchlocks, green banners, indigo head cloths). The sepia inset with its hard border reads clearly as Colachel: palms, powder smoke, spearmen and Nairs in one line. There is no text. Minor points: one musketman at top right wears a maroon head cloth, though red is reserved for Ponnan, and the stool is plainer than the carved one in 4.1. The three balloons fit in the open sky at upper centre (x 0.25 to 0.70, y 0 to 0.2) and the low-detail hills below it. The caption sits in the inset's sky.

Minor only. The raja is visible small and far off on his stool, though the prompt said he is outside the frame. That fits the valley geography, so I let it stand. The slow-match is drawn smouldering at the musket muzzles, not at the wrists. A few spearmen wear thin shoulder straps. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud, thick moustache, clean chin, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth and silver chain. Kayal's ochre-bay head with black mane is in the foreground. The open sky at top centre takes both Nagoji balloons.

Usable, with minor issues. Nagoji is seen past his shoulder, mounted on the ochre-bay Kayal, but he and the horse face into the scene toward his own column, so the raja's point of view is loose. The present-day Padmini shows black hair with no visible grey (the prompt asked for black). The quiet band above the inset is tight. The letterer should use the pale sky strip at the top of the inset (about x 0.63-0.86, y 0.61-0.70) and the empty road between Kayal's head and the inset (about x 0.51-0.62, y 0.63-0.95) for the two remembered lines, keeping both young faces clear. The inset itself works: young Padmini with black hair points her stick at a leaner young Kollamkara with gold ear hoops, chains, a gold-edged sash and a sword. The Travancore musketeers and the bullock-drawn gun match page 4.

Minor only. The slow-match on the slope muskets burns at the muzzle tips instead of at the wrists. The raja matches his bible line: heavy and bare-chested, gold hoops and chains, gold-edged sash, sword at the sash, long loose curls like 5.1 and 5.4. His shoulders are tight and he glances sideways, which is the script beat. Nagoji is off panel, so his two tails point to the left edge, matching his position on the left in 5.4. There is a large empty sky for all three balloons.

Minor only. List one for the author. Nagoji's gold ear ornament is a stud with a tiny bead hanging below it (about 10 px tall, at x 0.32, y 0.10), not a fully flush stud. It only shows when zoomed; at print size it reads as a gold dot. The same tiny drop was on r2 v02. One background spearman at right (x 0.86) wears a rust-coloured head cloth and an orange-brown mundu. That is close to the 'no red' rule, but it sits in the earth-brown range, and rust head cloths also appear in 5.1. Everything else matches. Nagoji is mounted on Kayal with: Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, silver chain, the cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth over ONE shoulder, bare arms and a white mundu. That matches 5.1 and 5.5 and fixes the r1 and r2 costume faults. His visible right forearm is unmarked. Kayal is an ochre bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings. The raja sits on his carved stool looking up at Nagoji: heavy and bare-chested, with long loose curls, gold hoops and chains, the gold-edged sash and the sword at the sash. His men wear indigo or earth-brown, the banners are plain green, and there is no text. The open sky at upper centre-right (about x 0.47-0.95, y 0.02-0.28) holds both balloons. Put the raja's line first.

Minor only. Soft smoke drifts from the muzzles of the aiming musketmen on both slopes; it can read as a recent shot, though there is no muzzle flash. The raja sits behind Nagoji rather than facing him, a common foreground-speaker staging. Nagoji's head sits in the upper half of the strip with the topknot touching the top edge, so do not crop from the top. Nagoji is close and level: topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud, thick curled moustache, smooth clean chin, cream gold-bordered shoulder cloth and silver chain. Open sky at upper centre-right takes the balloon.

Minor only: some of the raja's spearmen wear orange turbans and one has a rust-orange waistband (saffron, not Ponnan's red); Nagoji's chain of office is drawn as a silver coin necklace rather than a plain chain. Nagoji matches the sheet and chapter row (topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, no turban or sash); Kayal is a bay with black mane and lower legs; the raja is bare-chested in gold-edged sash, ear hoops, neck chains, sword at sash, hand on the stool as he pushes up. Setting and lighting match the page 5 frames. Open sky between the two green banners (upper centre) takes both balloons. No text, gore or anachronism.

Acceptable. The wide shot works: the raja waves a raised hand while his spearmen stand in two lines with the road open down the middle. The banners are plain green, there is no text and no blood, the hands are sound, and the open sky gives plenty of room for both of his balloons. One minor continuity drift: here the raja has a short dark chin beard and a small red dot on his forehead. In 5.2 to 5.4 and in 6.1 he has a moustache and stubble only. The bible sets no beard rule for him. A few spearmen also wear olive-green cloth and head cloths, where the bible asks for indigo or earth-brown.

Acceptable, and it fixes everything flagged in r1/r2. Ponnan matches his sheet: curly hair with no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth over a short red jacket with gold trim, white mundu and a spear. He turns and leans toward Nagoji. Nagoji on Kayal matches the chapter 23 row: topknot, grey temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging from it, silver chain and white mundu with shoulder cloth. His visible right forearm is plain skin. Kayal is bay with a black mane. Ponnan's horse sits somewhat lower. Spear points crowd in close on both sides. The raja's men are bare-chested in indigo and earth-brown with indigo and brown head cloths and round dark shields, under plain green banners. The raja stands small in the far distance beside his stool: bare-chested, bare-headed, moustache and no beard, white mundu with a gold sash. This matches 6.1 and 6.2. There is no painted text, gore or anachronism. Lettering space: the clear sky across the top centre (about x 0.28 to 0.6, y 0 to 0.17) holds all three items. The caption can run across the top over the banners, Ponnan's balloon can sit above his head and Nagoji's to the left of his topknot. Minor points: a few small matchlock men on the slopes wear indigo shirts rather than going bare-chested, but they read as local cloth, not blue coats. Both riders wear dark boots in the stirrups. Ponnan's horse is only modestly smaller than Kayal.

Clean and on script. The wide high-ridge view shows thick black smoke columns over torched pepper gardens and support poles along a canal. Raiders in plain earth-brown and cream cloth with indigo head cloths walk away unhurried down a scrub path at right. There are no bodies, no red cloth, no muskets or blue coats, and no painted text. The smoke-dimmed grey sky across the top band, especially the paler haze at upper left and centre, holds all three captions. Two minor points: the raiders wear plain shirts rather than going bare-chested, and the two nearest are somewhat close to the ridge rather than far below, but both still read as small, distant figures.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet and the chapter 16 to 27 row: cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no blouse, gold ear studs and necklace, grey threading through her black hair, and her long walking stick gripped hard in her right hand while her left hand is clenched. The burned gardens read clearly: torched vines, cut poles and trampled red soil, with the canal at left. Two men lie still, with no wounds, and a farmer draws a cloth over one. The raiders are small on the far ridge. The dark smoke sky above and right of her head leaves room for her two balloons and the caption. Minor: the farmer wears a stitched olive short-sleeved shirt with rolled sleeves where a shoulder cloth would be more typical, and Padmini's hair sits loose and curly rather than in a clear coil at the nape.

Minor issues, acceptable. The gun locks are generic and show no slow-match, but none is clearly a flintlock or percussion lock. The grey-horse rider is falling back, hands at his chest, rather than fully thrown clear. On the cream horse, the rider's foot caught in the stirrup is readable but not emphatic. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Minor: Nagoji wears tall black riding boots here, while in panel 7.5 they are dark brown ankle boots. Nagoji is otherwise on model: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, flush ear stud, silver chain. Kayal has no white markings.

Acceptable, with minor issues. Ponnan matches his sheet (curly hair, moustache, clean chin, red gold-trimmed jacket and red shoulder cloth, white mundu at bare knees). His horse is a bay with a white star, distinct from Kayal. The cut stirrup strap is implied rather than shown. The tiny far body in the road has an odd leg arrangement and a red waist cloth, so it reads more like a fallen rider than the bare-chested shooter. Three ambushers at top left are still firing. The flank riders at right show their backs as well as the spear points. There is no blood, no text, and no lettering is needed.

Minor: Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold bead that sits just below the lobe. It reads as a stud at page size. Background Travancore riders and one dead ambusher wear small, dull maroon waist cloths, which slightly dilute 'red cloth is Ponnan's alone'. They are small and do not compete with Ponnan's red. The face-down dead ambushers at lower right show no blood.

Clean. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain of office, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash, and a pale scar line on the inner left forearm. Kayal is correct (bay, black mane, black lower legs, ochre quilted pad). Ponnan has curly hair, moustache, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear, bare knees, on a smaller horse. Late-afternoon ridge over thorn and rock valley, gun cart and riders behind. Minor only: one tiny background man on the right wears a red head cloth, and Ponnan seems to have a small ear stud that is not on his sheet. Open sky top right and above Ponnan takes the balloon.

Clean. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch16-27 row: black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape, gold ball earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border, no blouse, and a long walking stick in her right hand. She rides at the rear of the column with a hard, flinty look. The bullock-drawn gun and the riders lead away along the ridge, and the late-afternoon sky gives wide clear space at the top and upper right for all three balloons. Nagoji is off panel, so his tail goes to the right edge toward the head of the column.

Acceptable. Nagoji's Kerala topknot has grey at the temples, with no turban and no sash. He wears a white mundu with a gold-bordered shoulder cloth and a silver chain. His moustache is thick and curled, his chin clean-shaven, and a small gold bead sits at the ear lobe. Sweating crew haul on the rope, and the gun captain sights along the barrel at the scrub valley. One minor flaw: the gun captain's face nearly touches the cascabel, which reads a little awkward but still says 'sighting'. The sky at the upper right and centre is open for Nagoji's balloon. The sunset light matches 8.2.

Acceptable. This wide shot carries the full beat: the gunner touches the linstock to the vent, flame bursts from the muzzle, a great bank of smoke rolls out, and a flock of birds bursts up over the trees across the thorn valley. The crew are sound, there is no text and no gore, and the large open sky across the top suits the long caption. Two minor flaws. The sky is bluer and brighter than the sunset glow of 8.2 and 8.3, though warm light still shows on the right horizon. The bullock yoke is still hitched just behind the gun carriage.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches sheet and ch23 row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, white mundu, no turban or sash. He is on foot with his talwar drawn, leading spearmen down off the ridge into the thorn, with the gun and riders left on the crest. Hands and sword grip are sound. Minor: a small rider top left wears a rust-red turban, and the small spearman at lower right wears a red head cloth. Both are against the chapter's red-for-Ponnan rule, but they are distant, and Nagoji is unmistakably the foreground figure. Open sky top right takes both the 'Now.' balloon and the caption.

Minor only: the light is a little brighter than the script's 'dim', and the ball is drawn still in flight next to leaves it has already shredded. Nagoji is on model: topknot, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, white mundu with shoulder cloth, silver chain, no turban or sash. The raider in the background with an indigo head cloth and matchlock is acceptable. No text, no blood, and the hands are sound.

Minor: the elbow is already touching the spearman's jaw, slightly past 'the instant before contact'. Otherwise the beat reads well: the spear point scrapes past his hip as he twists into the elbow strike. Nagoji is on model (topknot, grey temples, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, mundu), and the faint pale scar shows on the inner left forearm. Both men's hands have five fingers and are correct. No text or blood.

Clean. Two dark silhouettes stand against a wall of white powder smoke. Rim light picks out the ash smeared on the raider's face as he holds his sword high, and Nagoji steps inside the swing. Nagoji keeps his topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin and gold stud. In the background a third raider with a dagger slips as loose stones scatter. Torn cloth strips flutter from the raider's arm, which reads as plausible. No text, no blood, and the setting matches the neighbouring panels.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the lock: hair gathered into a topknot on the crown, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin (soot specks only), small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth over the LEFT shoulder (consistent with 9.1). He is drawn chest-up and close with soot and sweat. The three raiders lie still behind him with no wounds: the spearman left, the swordsman centre, the dagger man right. Minor points: (1) the topknot is looser than in 9.1, with more hair hanging at the sides; (2) the dead raiders are rendered sharp rather than in soft focus; (3) the left spearman's spear butt disappears behind his head (it reads as planted in the ground, not as a wound, but the letterer could check it at print size); (4) the shoulder cloth here is plain white, without the gold border seen in 9.1. For the two captions, the top-right corner over the cliff and smoke (about x 0.66 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.20) is clear and covers no face or key action. The top-left thorn corner is a second option.

Clean. The boy is thin and beardless with a small hair knot and a torn brown shoulder cloth. He is backed against a pale rock face, holds no sword, raises both hands (five fingers each) and shows terror in his wide eyes. A large, low-detail stretch of rock wall at the upper right gives room for the BOY balloon. No text, no blood, and no other figures.

Minor: the talwar is in his right hand here but in his left in 10.4. The fallen raiders lie on muted red-brown cloth that does not read as blood. The silver chain has a different link and pendant design from 10.2 and 10.4. Identity is clean: topknot, grey temples, tiny flush gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, soot streaks. Open sky at upper right takes the caption and Nagoji's balloon.

Minor: the forearm scar on his raised LEFT arm is pinkish instead of white and sits near the elbow. The boy's hair reads as a messy crown bun plus a small knot at the nape. Matches the beat: a low angle from behind the boy, talwar high against a white sky, the boy shrinking with his hands up. The large white sky at upper right takes the caption.

None significant. A tight insert: Ponnan's arm, in a red short sleeve with a gold border and with the edge of the red shoulder cloth, enters from the right and clamps Nagoji's wrist just above the hilt. Nagoji's forearm shows the long pale scar running along it. Ponnan entering from the right matches his screen position in 10.4. Open sky at upper left takes the off-panel balloon, with its tail toward the top-right corner.

Minor: the brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is a small dark ink blot, not a pale puckered patch. It is on the correct arm, with the pale scar running along the forearm. Three hands are stacked on the wrist and hilt, and they resolve correctly. Ponnan matches his sheet: curly hair with no topknot, red jacket and shoulder cloth, hitched mundu, bare knees, soot on the face. Nagoji has a cocked right fist, ready to strike. The sky at upper right and the foliage band at upper left take the two short balloons.

Minor: the sword's hilt is a straight cross-guard with ball ends and a round pommel, and the blade is straight. In 10.3 and 10.4 it is a curved talwar with a knuckle-bow. This is a prop continuity slip, not an anachronism. The shot is a close two-shot rather than a single close-up on Ponnan, but his speaking face is large, his mouth is open mid-word and his grip on the wrist is clear. The rest is clean. Nagoji is on the left and Ponnan on the right, which matches 10.3 and 10.4. Nagoji is on-model: topknot with grey temples, a tiny flush gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin with only soot shading, silver chain on a bare soot-streaked chest, cream shoulder cloth and the pale scar on his inner LEFT forearm. Ponnan is on-model: curly hair with no topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, soot on the face, red short jacket with gold-trimmed sleeves, red shoulder cloth and white mundu.
